slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
disgustingly intelligent

a tiny blog

write one short post a week explaining something you just learned, even if nobody reads it. writing it out shows you exactly what you understood and what you only thought you did.

an instrument, badly

spend 15 minutes a day learning an instrument, even badly. music trains memory, patience and pattern recognition at the same time, and almost nothing else does all three.

fixing things yourself

once a month, fix or build one thing yourself instead of buying it: a shelf, a bike tyre, a lamp. understanding how things work makes you sharper than any quiz ever could.

one era a week

pick one era a week, ancient egypt, the renaissance, the space race, and spend 5 minutes a day on it. by sunday you can talk about it better than most people ever will.
slides.texte_sophia:
one era a week

pick one era a week, ancient egypt, the renaissance, the space race, and give it 5 minutes a day. a micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, and by sunday you can talk about it.

slides.texte_overlay:
a useless language

spend 10 minutes a day on a language you'll probably never need. a new language rewires how you think about your own, and people light up when you try to speak theirs.
